page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-128 is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the Standard server family. It is built around the AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at a frequency of 2.55 GHz. The allocation provides 8 dedicated physical cores with two threads per core, yielding 16 total vCPUs. Because CPU resources are provisioned on dedicated hardware rather than shared pools, execution threads avoid the CPU credit and throttling constraints associated with burstable instance models.

The instance features 128 GB of total system memory, equating to 8.0 GB per core. This creates an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, aligning the configuration with memory-heavy computing patterns. Hardware acceleration is absent, with a GPU count of zero. Additionally, the instance provisions no integrated local storage disks, meaning persistent storage must be attached via remote block volumes. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for ingress and egress routing.

From a resource allocation standpoint, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-128 trades integrated low-latency disk IOPS for elevated memory density relative to core count. The absence of onboard NVMe drives reduces overall infrastructure cost per gigabyte of memory, making it structurally efficient for RAM-dependent tasks that rely on decoupled storage architectures. Suitable workloads include in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, backend API processing, and large ETL data transformation pipelines that fit within a 128 GB working set.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-128 is a flexible compute instance configured for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by AMD EPYC 7J13 processors based on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.55 GHz and 16 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 128 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio that yields 8.0 GB of RAM per compute unit. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs, nor does it include bundled local storage disks, necessitating reliance on networked storage attachments for data persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided as standard network infrastructure. With its dedicated core execution model and substantial RAM capacity, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.8-128 functions effectively for memory-optimized use cases such as in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large dataset ETL jobs, and enterprise application servers requiring predictable execution without local disk overhead.
